title: The Gray Reach
intro: The barrow on the hill above Last Light has opened, and a gray blight creeps down the Vale of Ash — crops first, then cattle, then the will to stay. Someone must go up and settle the Hollow King, by verse or by crown or by steel. The Vale is one hold of nine. What you learn under that hill is only the beginning of it. Ask people more than one thing; carry what they give you; choose, and live with it.

objectives.text: Act 3: Marrowgate. The Hollow Throne lies under the palace. Fill it with the rite (three holds rested, the Vale's king at rest, the first Reeve's confession), burn it with Ironbound oil, sit in it with a crown, or read the founding ledger aloud to those who trust you — each is an ending, and the seat can be weighed before choosing. Kneeling to it ends your story. Companions can be met in the Vale and asked to come along, as many as will. Reputation with the Watch, the Church, the Ironbound, the Free Companies, the Keepers, and the Crown opens and closes doors.

Act 2: the holds. Six holds, six unrested griefs, each to be rested, bargained with, or burned. Coldpass opens on three hollows rested (the Keepers' stair), the Regent's writ (two hollows burned, or two services to Highward's Watch), or the Free Companies' word (Gullhaven or Camp Gallows). The realm is large: the straight road to Marrowgate runs near three hundred turns; seeing every hold whole, many times that. Companions can be met in the Vale and asked to come along, as many as will. Reputation with the Watch, the Church, the Ironbound, the Free Companies, the Keepers, and the Crown opens and closes doors.

Act 1: settle the Hollow King in the barrow north of the Vale — speak his three verses, return his crown, or end him. Then the roads open: six holds, each with its own unrested grief, and the pass to Marrowgate beyond. Companions can be met in the Vale and asked to come along, as many as will. Reputation with the Watch, the Church, the Ironbound, the Free Companies, the Keepers, and the Crown opens and closes doors. Kneeling to the king ends your story. The realm is large: the straight road to Marrowgate runs near three hundred turns; seeing every hold whole, many times that.

warden.name: Warden
warden.desc: a soldier of the old watch — strong, hard to kill; steel opens what words and lore cannot

scout.name: Scout
scout.desc: quick and quiet — locks, ledges, and carved stone all give to careful hands (grace)

scholar.name: Scholar
scholar.desc: reads the old tongue outright — verses, ledgers, and the dead's own words come easy (wits)

envoy.name: Envoy
envoy.desc: a silver tongue — talks open doors, coffers, and grudges that iron cannot (will)

stages.text: Marrowgate. The Hollow Throne lies under the palace; the Regent will not want you there.
Three hollows rested: the pilgrim stair at Coldpass opens for you. Highward's north road leaves from its record-house.
The Regent's writ is yours. Coldpass will let you through to Marrowgate.
The Free Companies will take you under the pass, by the Saltkerns caves.
Six holds, six unrested griefs. Rest three, earn the Regent's writ, or buy the Companies' road — any opens Coldpass.
The king rests. See who comes to Last Light square now that he does.
The king is dust. See who comes to Last Light square now that he is.
You left him grieving. See who comes to Last Light square anyway.
The gray runs through nine holds. Settle the Vale's king first; then the roads open.

act1.name: Act I — The Vale of Ash

stages.text: Settle the Hollow King: speak his verses, return or break his crown, or end him. The doors after are yours too.
The barrow is open. Hear the king at the throne before you decide anything.
Settle the Hollow King in the barrow north of the Vale. Last Light knows the roads; its people know more.

epilogue.text: In the Vale the barrow doors stay shut, as you promised, and white grass grows back over the hill.
In the Vale the barrow doors stay shut, as you chose, and white grass grows back over the hill.
In the Vale the barrow stands open to the sky, and the gray priest goes up on feast days to sit with the king.
In the Vale they tell it that a stranger killed the Hollow King with a blade, and the grass came back gray-green and stayed so.
In the Vale the king still sits his stone seat, grieving. The gray there never fully lifts.
The iron crown lies in pieces on the barrow floor. No one has tried to mend it.
The Hollow King's crown is in your pack still. It has not grown lighter.

states.text: trusted — gates and escorts open to you
wary — they hold you longer at every gate
in your debt — doors, rites, and secrets open to you
cold — the Church remembers what you did
counted a brother — fire and iron yours to ask for
despised — they will not arm you
a friend of the Companies — passage and favours
marked — the Companies remember a wrong
one of theirs — the old rites and roads are yours
turned away — they will not teach you
in the Regent's memory, and not kindly
